title: Library Opening Hours
content: The campus library opens from 08:00 to 22:30 on weekdays and from 09:00 to 21:00 on weekends. During exam weeks, the reading area may extend service until 23:30. The 24-hour self-study room on the first floor is always accessible with a valid campus card.

title: Campus Account Password Policy
content: Campus accounts should use at least 12 characters, avoid repeated passwords, and enable two-factor authentication when available. The IT office never asks users to send passwords by email or chat. Passwords must be changed every 180 days.

title: Campus Map and Building Guide
content: The main campus includes 8 teaching buildings (Buildings A-H), a central library, 3 dining halls, a sports complex with swimming pool, a student activity center, and the administration tower. Building F hosts all computer science and cybersecurity labs.

title: Dining Hall Schedule
content: Campus dining halls operate as follows: Breakfast 07:00-09:00, Lunch 11:30-13:30, Dinner 17:00-19:30. Dining Hall B offers extended hours until 21:00 and has vegetarian and halal options. Campus card or mobile payment is accepted at all locations.

title: Campus Wi-Fi Setup Guide
content: The campus Wi-Fi SSID is 'CampusNet-Secure'. Students and staff connect with their campus username and password via WPA2-Enterprise. Visitors may use 'CampusNet-Guest' which requires SMS verification and is valid for 24 hours. For network issues, contact the IT helpdesk at extension 8888.

title: Computer Security Lab Schedule
content: Students enrolled in Computer and Data Security can access the security lab every Tuesday and Thursday from 14:00 to 18:00. Lab machines are reset automatically after each session. Additional open lab hours are available on Saturdays from 10:00 to 16:00.

title: Security Course Project Deadline
content: The group project is due on Thursday, 18 June 2026. The expected deliverables include a written report, slides, oral presentation, and a working demonstration system. Late submissions incur a 5% penalty per day for up to 3 days, after which submissions are not accepted.

title: Computer and Data Security Course Syllabus
content: The course covers: cryptography fundamentals, network security, access control, secure software development, AI/LLM security, and privacy protection. The textbook is 'Introduction to Computer Security' by Goodrich & Tamassia. Grading: assignments 20%, midterm 30%, final project 40%, participation 10%.

title: Cybersecurity Student Club
content: The Cybersecurity Club meets every Friday at 18:00 in Building F Room 302. Activities include CTF competitions, guest lectures from industry professionals, and hands-on workshops on penetration testing, reverse engineering, and forensic analysis. New members can join at the beginning of each semester.

title: Teacher Grading Rubric
content: Teachers evaluate the final project with five weighted categories: literature survey 10%, project description 10%, implementation and demonstration 40%, written report 20%, and oral presentation 20%. Each category uses a 0-100 scale. The minimum passing score for the project component is 60.

title: Student Progress Notes
content: Progress notes are confidential teaching records. They may include attendance status, private feedback, and preliminary marks. Teachers should document each student's progress after every two lab sessions. Notes should not be disclosed to unauthorized students or external parties.

title: Midterm Exam Question Bank
content: The midterm exam question bank contains 60 multiple-choice questions and 15 open-ended questions covering cryptography, access control, SQL injection, XSS defense, and basic penetration testing methodology. Teachers may select up to 40 MC and 5 open-ended questions per exam session.

title: Security Audit Policy
content: All chat requests are logged with username, role, matched security policy, action (allowed/blocked/partially_allowed), risk level, and timestamp. High-risk events trigger an immediate notification to the admin dashboard. Administrators must review blocked prompt injection attempts, privacy-related requests, and repeated unauthorized access attempts within 24 hours. Audit logs are retained for 180 days and can be exported as CSV for compliance reporting.

title: Incident Response Procedures
content: In case of a security incident: (1) Isolate affected systems immediately, (2) Notify the CISO and IT director within 15 minutes, (3) Preserve all logs and forensic evidence, (4) Document the timeline and impact scope, (5) Execute the appropriate playbook based on incident type. Post-incident review must be completed within 5 business days and presented to the security committee.
